category_review.rationale: Interactive science lesson explaining noise cancellation with a wave simulation and quiz.
category_review.evidence: A single-page scrollytelling science explainer titled 'Silence, made of sound', published by the invented magazine [BRAND]. It explains how [DEVICE] cancel [NOISE_SOURCE] in four chapters. (1) Sound as a pressure wave: a sticky live canvas changes state with each scroll step. (2) The anti-noise phase lab: the reader drags a coral anti-noise wave or a 0–360° slider, and the summed wave flattens at 180° while a live readout shows the resulting level. (3) Inside the earcup: a hand-drawn SVG cut-away builds up part by part with numbered callouts. (4) Limits: an animated SVG bar chart of active versus passive cancellation by frequency. A four-question quiz with instant feedback closes the page. Everything is drawn in Canvas 2D or inline SVG. There is no audio, no microphone and no images.

category_review.rationale: Interactive science explanation of carbon flows and emissions scenarios.
category_review.evidence: A single-page illustrated scroll story by [BRAND], a small independent science explainer studio, about [TOPIC]. One large code-drawn SVG cross-section (sky, land with forest and mountains, open ocean, rock strata with fossil seams) is moving from the first frame: glowing particles stream between the four reservoirs ([RESERVOIRS]) along curved paths, with speed and density showing the size of each flow ([FLOWS]). The scene stays pinned while text steps scroll past and the camera pans and zooms from reservoir to reservoir. The fourth, human-driven flow starts as a thin thread and thickens through the industrial era. A yearly ledger follows, then a scenario lab: a slider with three stops ([SCENARIOS]) that smoothly redraws a curve of [OUTCOME], updates a big readout and shifts the sky tint. Every figure is tagged Illustrative and a closing sources note explains the rounding.

category_review.evidence: A single-page interactive science explainer by [BRAND] on how [TOPIC] works. category_review.rationale: Astronomy lesson demonstrating planetary scales in an interactive model.

The signature moment is the scale switch: when distances and sizes animate to their true proportions, the planets all but vanish, and a live readout says how many pixels wide [HOME_BODY] now is.

category_review.rationale: Step-by-step computing lesson following an HTTPS request.
category_review.evidence: A single-page scrollytelling explainer published by Northbeam Primers that follows one HTTPS request for https://kettleandcrumb.example/recipes/rye-sourdough from a laptop to an origin server and back. Seven full-height scenes (request, DNS lookup, router hops on an abstract dotted map, TCP handshake, TLS and the lock, the server's reply in packets, rendering) each pair three short reading beats with a sticky code-drawn SVG diagram and exactly one hands-on control. A header rail tracks the packet's stage and a running round-trip timer; a fast replay and a 14-term glossary close the story. When the variables change, all copy and sample data are rewritten to fit them; keep everything in src/content.ts.

category_review.rationale: Financial literacy lesson using an interactive compound-interest calculator.
category_review.evidence: A single-page interactive explainer published by [BRAND] that teaches compound interest to [AUDIENCE]. The hero is a working calculator: sliders for monthly deposit, annual rate and years drive a large hand-drawn SVG stacked area chart (deposits vs. interest) and an animated final-balance counter. Below it, scrollytelling chapters with a sticky chart explain compounding step by step, a 'start at [START_AGES]' scene compares two savers, an inflation toggle reframes every figure in today's money, and a formula corner shows the math with live values. Every figure is a labeled hypothetical; the page never gives advice.

category_review.rationale: Interactive computing explainer showing next-token prediction.
category_review.evidence: A single long-scroll interactive explainer for [BRAND] titled "[TOPIC]". One unfinished example sentence, [EXAMPLE_SENTENCE], travels through a pinned SVG stage in eight steps while short caption cards scroll past: the sentence splits into token chips, the chips get numeric ids, the chips fly onto a 2D meaning map with labeled regions, curved attention arcs connect each word to the earlier words it relies on, a bar chart shows the top eight candidate next words, and a temperature slider with a seeded dice roll samples an ending the reader can re-roll. It closes with a five-icon recap strip, a glossary, a short FAQ and a footer. No model runs in the browser: every number is invented, illustrative and stored in one content file.

category_review.rationale: Marine science lesson explaining ocean depth zones and their organisms.
category_review.evidence: A single-page interactive explainer for [BRAND] called [TITLE]: one very tall scroll is a dive through [SUBJECT], from 0 m at the surface down to the bottom of the last zone in [ZONES]. A full-screen intro shows the waterline. Then the dive section maps scroll to depth: every zone in [ZONES] gets an equal share of the scroll and depth runs linearly inside each share. A fixed depth gauge shows the live metre readout, the zone name, light, pressure and temperature. The page background color is interpolated by depth from sunlit cyan to near-black. Two short serif chapters per zone fade in and out on alternating sides. Six real public-domain NOAA photographs pass as framed plates in the first three zones and desaturate as the water darkens. A canvas draws marine snow, surface light shafts, jellyfish, a lanternfish school and an anglerfish that react to the cursor, and a seafloor at the bottom. The page ends on the seafloor with one glowing organism the visitor can press and hold to make it flare, followed by a visit line and a button back to the surface. Static site, no backend, no audio.

category_review.rationale: Computing lesson comparing deterministic sorting steps and complexity.
category_review.evidence: [BRAND] is a single-page, browser-only sorting lab. The working visualizer is the first screen: a large canvas bar stage with its transport controls attached, and no marketing hero in front of it. Bubble, insertion, merge, quick and heap sort each precompute a full list of steps, so play, pause, step forward, step back, scrub and reset are all deterministic. Below the stage come complexity cards with counts measured on the current array, a race mode that runs two algorithms on one array and one clock, a table of step totals per input pattern, and short notes on reading the numbers.
